pr_title: STM32 UART: Request RX data flush on async_rx_enable
pr_comments: Thanks @bjarki-trackunit. Can you have a look to https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/65320 ?
Very interesting, I haven't noticed this issue. I got the one additional byte only if any transfer happens before enabling the async transfer. Maybe it is chip dependent problem.

issue_context.title: stm32 async uart: unknown state of the module while enabling transfer
issue_context.body:
Actually, I'm not sure if it's a bug or a feature :-) feel free to change the label.

The UART module is enabled at `PRE_KERNEL_1` level. Let's assume the `uart_rx_enable` (enabling async transfer) function is called at `POST_KERNEL` level. It can't be called earlier, because of some dependencies. There is a window when UART module is enabled, but the async transfer not. If we receive a byte or two in this window the RXNE bit will be set (and potentially overrun). Then, when the DMA is enabled, it will copy the one byte from the DR register (because RXNE is set), but an interrupt won't be trigger, because an IDLE line is not detected. When the next transfer occurs, the interrupt will be triggered and pass all new data with the one byte from the previous transfer at the beginning. 

I think it is a bit misleading. Do you think it is intended behavior?

IMO, there are two possible solutions for that:
1. Clear the RXNE (and maybe errors) bit in the UART driver, before enabling DMA not to copy data received before enabling async transfer.
2. Do not change the current implementation and assume it is up to the driver user to read the register (and clear errors?) with `uart_poll_in` which clears the RXNE flag.

Please let me know what you think.
comments:
I can think of two other ways to deal with this (in addition to the one mentioned above):

* Enable hardware flow control on both end, and de-assert CTS so the other end does not send anything until you are ready. Though it will still receive whatever is at the other end waiting in queue. Or,
* You can always clear out the input (e.g. by doing polling in until there is nothing to be received) before enabling async transfer.

But I think it is really up to the user of async transfer to decide what to do, as it will require both ends to agree to some handshaking before exchanging any data.

Thanks for the response :-)

>Enable hardware flow control on both end, and de-assert CTS so the other end does not send anything until you are ready. Though it will still receive whatever is at the other end waiting in queue. Or,

Unfortunately, I can't change how the transmitter works, so enabling flow control isn't an option in my case.

 >You can always clear out the input (e.g. by doing polling in until there is nothing to be received) before enabling async transfer.

It is 2 solution from my first comment, right? Or I'm missing something.

So, you think adding clearing `RXNE` flag in the `uart_stm32_async_rx_enable` function (inside the driver) is not a good option?

I am not sure about the STM32 hardware. But if there is a way to tell the hardware to discard buffered input (or even simply reset the hardware to clear out everything), that would work better/faster than clearing by doing polling-in.

Also, correct me if I am wrong, even if you clear `RXNE` in `uart_stm32_async_rx_enable`, there is still data in the FIFO, so the interrupt will still fire, right?

The async mode always works with DMA. The `RXNE` bit is a trigger for DMA to copy data from `DR` (data register) to a provided buffer during configuration. When new data is received and RXNE is cleared by DMA, `DR` register content is just replaced with the new byte.
![image](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/72437029/6fc47dc9-d466-4dca-b80e-46d4be734059)

However, you are right. There are some STM32 chips e.g. STM32H7 that can use FIFO embedded in the UART module. When the FIFO mode is enabled, the `RXFNE` (RX FIFO not empty) is a trigger for the DMA. With FIFO disabled it is also `RXNE`. But the current STM32 driver doesn't support enabling FIFO mode, so there is no need to clear that bit at the moment.

Regarding interrupt - the async mode uses IDLE line interrupt. The interrupt is triggered after transfer, when the IDLE line is detected. The `RXNE` is used only to trigger DMA transfer, after every byte.

I don't have a good generic solution...

As for your application, do you know if the transmitter has flow control enabled at all? Or does it disregard any CTS/RTS and simply keeps on sending stuff? Although you can't change the transmitting side, maybe they have already enabled flow control.
Unfortunately, it is not enabled. In my opinion, clearing RXNE is a good solution. I've sent PR #64950 to present that.

> I don't know why LL_USART_DisableDMAReq_RX isn't called in uart_stm32_dma_rx_disable. At the first glance it should be. However DMA is disabled with dma_stop, so data are not copied after every received byte and the DMAR bit is set in the uart_stm32_async_rx_enable function anyway.

@FRASTM can answer maybe ?

review_comments: Not all STM32 chips has this function. You need probably `#ifdef USART_RQR_RXFRQ`. I guess  `LL_USART_ClearFlag_RXNE` is required in the `#else` part.
Well, `LL_USART_ReceiveData8` also fixes the issue, is that available to all chips?
I think so, you can check that in hal_stm32. But I don't know what happens when the UART has FIFO.Why don't you want to use `LL_USART_ClearFlag_RXNE` and `LL_USART_RequestRxDataFlush`?
I want to keep it simple :) introducing ifdefs (especially when not necessary) is the root of all evil :D

Agree, however it may be necessary here, because of FIFO (I'm not able to verify it). Anyway, #ifdef to flush the RX buffer is already done here https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/drivers/serial/uart_stm32.c#L1269. I suspect it is done this way for some reason.
